definition: When multiple similar objects are present, the one that differs from the rest will be most readily remembered and attended to.
application: The primary 'Explore Projects' CTA uses a high-contrast warm amber accent (#FFB547 in dark / #B93A0A in light) with hard offset drafting shadow, while secondary actions use subtle outline borders to channel primary attention without cognitive competition.

definition: Signifiers communicate where the action should take place and the expected outcome before the action is executed.
application: The resume download CTA explicitly indicates file format (PDF) and exact file size, preventing user hesitation about unexpected heavy downloads or unknown document types.

definition: The time required to rapidly move to a target area is a function of the ratio between the distance to the target and the width of the target.
application: All interactive elements, buttons, navigation links, and filter chips maintain an accessible touch target area of at least 44x44px, minimizing target acquisition error across desktop and touchscreens.

theorist: William Hick & Ray Hyman (1952) / George Miller (1956)
definition: Decision time increases logarithmically with the number and complexity of choices available. Working memory capacity is roughly 7 ± 2 chunks.
application: The top navigation bar is grouped into 5 primary semantic sections (About, Academic, Activities, Projects, Contact), reducing cognitive load and decision latency.

definition: The system should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within a reasonable time.
application: Theme toggles, HCI Lens activations, and filter selections produce immediate visual state shifts (under 100ms) with persisted localStorage preferences and accessible ARIA live announcements.

theorist: Ben Shneiderman (Eight Golden Rules of Interface Design)
definition: Provide rapid, incremental, reversible operations whose impact on the object of interest is immediately visible.
application: Tag chips allow instant multi-criteria filtering of projects with real-time count badges and live result announcements for assistive technologies, eliminating full page reloads.

theorist: Walter J. Doherty & Ahrvind J. Thadani (IBM, 1982)
definition: Productivity soars when a computer and its users interact at a pace (<400ms) that ensures neither has to wait on the other.
application: Command palette searching, lightbox expansions, and section jumps operate with instant sub-50ms local memory queries, maintaining continuous user engagement.

definition: Carefully prevent problems from occurring in the first place, or help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors without data loss.
application: The contact form enforces real-time inline semantic validation with accessible aria-errormessage bindings and preserves previously entered message text in state even if network transmission fails.
